title: Named by deeds (Exodus Rabbah 3:6)
hook: God tells Moses: I am named according to My deeds
tomorrow: why does Moses, of all people, stumble over words?

segments.voice: Yesterday: not even a thorn bush, no place empty of the Presence. Today, the voice in that bush gets asked its name.

At a retirement party, nobody reads out a résumé. They tell stories: she never missed one of my games; he always stopped to fix the neighbor's gate. The title fades, and the deeds become the name. At the burning bush, Moses asks the name question. When the people ask who sent me, what do I tell them?
screen: `NOBODY READS THE RÉSUMÉ.` → `THE DEEDS BECOME THE NAME.` → `WHO SENT ME?`

segments.voice: God's answer in Exodus is famous and mysterious: "I AM THAT I AM." Exodus Rabbah hears it as an answer about deeds. Rabbi Abba bar Mammel says: the Holy One told Moses, you want to know My name? I am called according to My deeds. When I judge the world, I'm called Elohim. When I go out against the wicked, Tzevaot, hosts. When I hold back judgment on people's wrongs, El Shaddai. And when I have mercy on My world, I'm called by the holy name, the one read aloud in prayer as Adonai. So I am that I am becomes: I am what I do. The names change because the deeds change. That turns a big question around. Asking God's name, in this midrash, means asking what God does. And if even God is known by deeds, it's no wonder people are too. A name, on this reading, isn't the label on the door. It's the shape of what someone keeps doing: the one who shows up, the one who fixes things, the one who forgives. Names get earned in the doing, a day at a time.
screen: `WHAT IS YOUR NAME?` · `CALLED BY MY DEEDS.` · `JUDGING, MERCY: DIFFERENT NAMES.` · `KNOWN BY WHAT YOU DO.` · then, large: `NAMED BY DEEDS.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind three people you love, one at a time. For each, skip the job or the title and name one thing they do, the deed you'd tell at their party, counting them on your fingers. Then, gently, wonder which deed you'd like to be named for.
Named by deeds: Exodus Rabbah's reading of I am that I am. God is called by what God does: judging, holding back, mercy.
Your line: named by deeds. A name gets earned in the doing. Day fifteen eighty.

howItsDone: Jewish prayer uses several names of God, and Jews traditionally do not pronounce the holy four-letter name, reading it aloud as Adonai in prayer and often as HaShem, the Name, outside it.

chat.meaning: Exodus Rabbah: I am called according to My deeds. If God is named by deeds, a person's stories are their name too.

Elohim.meaning: a name of God, tied in the midrash to judging

Tzevaot.meaning: hosts: a name of God tied to going out against wrong

El Shaddai.meaning: a name of God tied to holding back judgment

Adonai.meaning: Lord: how the holy name is read aloud in prayer

Rabbi Abba bar Mammel.meaning: the sage who says God is named by deeds
